newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA DECORATES COMMUNIST MAUSOLEUM AS DALMATION.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA DECORATES COMMUNIST MAUSOLEUM AS DALMATION.

text.p: A white marble Mausoleum which once housed the embalmed body of Bulgaria's first communist leader Georgi Dimitrov was covered with more than 100 black dalmation spots on Sunday as part of a film promotion.

The Bulgarian film distributor of the live-action re-make of Disney's classic "101 Dalmations", Suny Films, organised a Dalmation dog contest and a children's show in front of the monument to mark the film's premiere in Bulgaria this week.
"We wanted to take people's mind off everyday economic hardship and politics and have some fun," a Suny Films official, surrounded by several Dalmations, told Reuters.
Despite the unseasonally cold weather, hundreds of dog-lovers, children and adults gathered in central Sofia to chear some 100 contesting Dalmations.
"This is a good diversion from campaigning politicians and crisis-solution debates," said one Dalmation-owner as he groomed his dog before the show.
As early general elections due on April 19 approach political addreses and debates dominate local media.
Month-long street protests in January toppled the ruling ex-communist Socialist government after it lead the country into an unprecedented economic crisis.
Eight revolving-door governments have failed so far to find a new application for the Mausoleum which now is empty.
The remains of Dimitrov, founder of Bulgarian communism and its first communist prime minister, were removed and cremated seven years ago.

Transforming the air-conditioned underground tomb into a central bank vault or turning this former communist shrine into a discotheque were some of the projects submitted so far, but none were approved.
